tolerance_basis: NOTES §4 applies: max|out| = 0.1281 < 1, so a flat absolute threshold is meaningful. floor = numpy per-op fp16 simulation (1.221e-04 abs, 1.00 ULP) -> atol = 4x floor, rtol = 4*2^-11.
tolerance_revision: registered before the first board run of this op; derived from a device-independent fp16 floor + NOTES §10.1 (no post-hoc adjustment).  see docs/OP-qkv.md §5

fp16_floor.note: numpy per-op fp16 rounding simulation vs the exact golden; device-independent

input_choice.graph_input: post-input_layernorm hidden [8,896] (RMSNorm NOT in the graph)
input_choice.gamma: layer0.input_layernorm.weight, applied in the pre-graph norm (NOT folded into the FC weights)
input_choice.source: embed.weight rows for fixed TOKEN_IDS, fp16-stored, float64 norm
input_choice.why: RMSNorm has its own operator ticket + board evidence (docs/OP-rmsnorm.md); keeping it out keeps a failure single-cause.  Folding gamma into W was rejected because the numpy golden would then have to fold it too (one more way to be silently wrong).

weights.bias_note: Qwen2.5 q/k/v all have biases and config.json has no key for them; measured std 7.8 (q) / 29.8 (k) / 0.015 (v) >> weight std, so dropping them shifts the output by >> tolerance (docs/OP-weights.md §4)
weights.kv_width_note: k/v width is 128 = 2 KV heads x 64, NOT 896.  A 896-wide mis-wiring is a different op: see neg_width896/ (element count 7168 vs 1024)

rope.formula: out_lo = a*cos - b*sin ; out_hi = b*cos + a*sin
rope.table: const pre-computed sin/cos duplicated over heads [T,H,HD/2]; SIN/COS are rejected by the ncc importer
rope.static_note: T must be static because the tables are data
rope.dyn_alternative: a runtime input table costs +2 SliceLayers and a second input file (docs/OP-rope.md §4); not built here

decomposition.rank_note: output rank 3; rank > 4 is rejected by ncc and rank 4 costs ~4x layers for the same work (docs/OP-rope.md §5.3)
